title: Strange lights
description: Strange lights are appearing over the town

pitches.title: The Opening Act
pitches.text: The lights answer marching-band practice, but recordings reveal they keep correcting one particularly bad trumpet part. Ancient accounts identify the visitors as touring aliens who mistake rehearsals for an invitation to perform; their opening note would rupture every human lung. With promised agency linguists never answering, the investigators translate the warning through musical imitation and stage a deliberately terrible audition. The disappointed aliens cancel Earth’s gig, leaving a scathing review and one instrument that can safely play their lethal frequency.

pitches.title: Lanterns for the Missing
pitches.text: Every light stops over a house whose occupant has disappeared, while residents insist those people never existed. Following a discarded birthday card exposes a celestial scavenger that consumes people and their place in memory, leaving its glowing digestive organs overhead. The investigators preserve names by reading them over the town’s emergency speakers, forcing the creature to regurgitate its victims. It flees hungry; everyone remembers the missing neighbors, including their debts, and the team’s sole reimbursement is an unsolicited casserole.

pitches.title: The Sky Is Leaking
pitches.text: The lights fall into gardens as tiny suns, making tomatoes ripen instantly and tools melt. A broken weather balloon turns out to have punctured the translucent body of an enormous sleeping animal curled around the atmosphere; each light is a clot, and the balloon recovery firm has been harvesting them. The investigators return the stolen clots using the firm’s own launch equipment before the animal wakes and shakes Earth loose. The firm loses its miraculous energy contract, and the town spends winter eating suspiciously warm tomatoes.

pitches.title: Future Fireworks
pitches.text: The lights precisely trace tomorrow’s accidents, although residents interpret the displays as a tourist attraction. An investigator recognizes their own impending death in the pattern, then finds a retired emergency dispatcher communicating backward through an electrical storm. She is the lone survivor of a catastrophe caused by the town’s new power plant and has only one night left to change it. The team evacuates the plant and cuts its cooling test short; the lights become an ordinary sunset, erasing both disaster and the dispatcher’s warning career.

pitches.title: The False Rapture
pitches.text: People under the lights become weightless and start giving away their possessions, convinced an ascension is imminent. Footage shows the beams collecting laughter rather than souls: a stranded angel has mistaken the town’s sarcastic complaints for sincere requests to leave Earth. Its rescue vessel cannot carry bodies, only personalities. The investigators demonstrate the difference between wanting to die and wanting a day off by bringing the angel to a miserable staff meeting. It returns everyone intact and grants the town one actual paid holiday, terrifying local employers.

pitches.title: Night Shift Pollinators
pitches.text: The lights appear over streetlamps, then households wake to glowing eggs in their ceilings. A blacked-out warehouse contains enormous transparent moths that use artificial light to mistake buildings for flowers; the eggs will hatch into larvae that eat the electromagnetic field keeping local matter solid. The team discovers the moths navigate by the true moon and persuades the town to switch off everything for one night. The swarm leaves peacefully, while investigators spend the blackout manually answering complaints that HQ’s nonexistent pest department should have handled.

pitches.title: The Town in the Fishbowl
pitches.text: The lights stay fixed despite wind, and telescope images show enormous fingers behind them. A child’s missing goldfish has grown into a cosmic pet and is observing the town inside a bowl stolen from a vanished agency depot; the apparent stars are its aquarium toys. Each feeding brings a tide through downtown. The investigators reconstruct the owner’s familiar feeding whistle, coax the fish away, and smash the bowl’s miniature Earth replica to release the real town. The child wants compensation for her fish, which now occupies the moon’s far side.

pitches.title: Second-Hand Stars
pitches.text: Each light appears after somebody buys a cheap lamp at a clearance sale, and illuminated rooms become windows onto different historical nights. The lamps contain captive stars sold by a sorcerer who financed immortality by stripping constellations; opening all of them will collapse the town’s timeline into his private midnight. Rather than wait for a nonexistent temporal unit, the team returns the lamps to the sky during the sale’s grand finale. The sorcerer ages centuries in seconds, and the rescued stars spell a thank-you visible only from the parking lot.

pitches.title: The Search Party
pitches.text: The lights inspect dumpsters and swimming pools, ignoring military targets while abducting anything shaped like a jellyfish. The investigators trace their search to an alien teenager who escaped a family vacation and is hiding as a local convenience-store clerk. His parents plan to sterilize the town to shake him out. The team gets him to reveal himself by confronting the real reason he fled: he was promised a summer internship on a slave planet. They negotiate his first ordinary wage instead, and the embarrassed parents depart with several regrettable human souvenirs.

pitches.title: Light at the End of the World
pitches.text: The lights extinguish whenever someone dies, and the newest ones resemble the faces of recently born children. A dying universe is using Earth as its next incarnation, threading its inhabitants into human souls; completion will overwrite everyone’s identity. The team locates the final light inside a maternity ward and learns the incoming universe cannot survive without consent. They persuade its elderly collective consciousness to die rather than steal a future. The lights become one harmless meteor shower, and an investigator must explain why the saved world still has a parking ticket.

title: Concerned parent
description: Kids at school are behaving weirdly

pitches.title: The Eye Subscriber
pitches.adjustment: Expands the design document’s streamer draft into a resolved case.
pitches.text: Masked students mailed their eyes to a streamer after subtitles promised exclusive views, and the recovered eyes still follow his livestream. The broadcaster is a many-eyed exile using a mistranslated audience-growth charm to rebuild a body; each donor will eventually become one of its minds. The investigators confront it during a school watch party and exploit its dependence on engagement by persuading the children to genuinely lose interest. Its body unravels into the original eyes, which return to their owners, while the school bans masks and completely misses the actual issue.

pitches.title: Adults on Loan
pitches.text: Students suddenly speak like exhausted accountants, and homework contains details of divorces their parents never discussed. Interviews reveal an educational fundraiser swapped children’s minds with their own future adult selves, supposedly letting them see the value of studying. The organizer secretly intends to keep a younger body. The investigators expose that every altered future ends in his expanding youth business, then destroy the fundraiser’s shared portrait before the swaps stabilize. Childhood returns, but the children remember enough of adulthood to demand recess as a legally protected benefit.

pitches.title: The Substitute Species
pitches.text: The children are eerily polite, never blink during roll call, and have started planting desks in the playground. A substitute teacher is a fungal intelligence replacing pupils with harmless-looking spores while storing the originals under the gym. Its civilization regards independent children as lonely fragments that require reunion. The team discovers the copies cannot understand private jokes and uses a chaotic school talent show to break their shared concentration. The originals escape and the substitute is contained in the neglected staff-room fern, where it finally experiences an authentically hostile collective.

pitches.title: Tomorrow’s Detention
pitches.text: The pupils refuse to enter one classroom and apologize for an accident that has not happened. A class experiment created a repeating afternoon ending in a gas explosion; children remember each cycle while adults reset. The principal keeps resetting it deliberately because this is the first semester his test scores have risen. Investigators entering the loop follow the students’ accumulated evidence to the leaking boiler and stop both explosion and reset. The school finally reaches Friday, and the children’s punishment for missing homework is overturned by eighteen years’ worth of dated complaints.

pitches.title: The Quietest Protest
pitches.text: Kids stop talking and trade tooth-shaped tokens, while adults begin losing the ability to say no. An ancient playground spirit answered one child’s wish that grown-ups would listen, granting students commands in exchange for their voices. The most neglected pupils plan to silence the whole town permanently. The team discovers the tokens retain everything the children tried to tell adults, and plays them at a public meeting before breaking the spirit’s pact. Voices return when parents actually respond; the spirit takes the principal’s public-address system as a consolation prize.

pitches.title: The Extra Child
pitches.text: Teachers remember a universally beloved pupil who does not appear in photographs, while real students skip meals to bring him offerings. A grief-born imaginary friend has become tangible by consuming the attention owed to other children; soon forgotten pupils will vanish completely. The investigators trace him to a child whose sibling died, and realize killing him would erase her last memory of that sibling. They give him a single honest story instead of unlimited admiration, reducing him to a companion only she can see. The missing children return, furious nobody noticed their absence.

pitches.title: The Competitive Possession
pitches.text: Students suddenly excel in obscure skills, but quarrel over who gets to use the same hand. A trophy rescued from a demolished school holds generations of dead pupils who want one final chance to graduate; each exam gives them longer control of living bodies. The investigators uncover unfinished records and host a graduation for the spirits, only to learn the trophy’s founder trapped failing children deliberately. They force his ghost to award every diploma, freeing both generations. Living pupils lose the supernatural talents but retain a remarkable ability to detect a rigged institution.

pitches.title: The Recess Embassy
pitches.text: The schoolchildren hum in unison and carry lunches they never eat. Beneath a playground slide, an alien refugee larva has been exchanging dreams with them, and the children are sheltering it from adults they correctly expect to panic. Its pursuers arrive disguised as district inspectors and begin deleting witnesses. The team realizes the weird behavior is a children's evacuation plan, helps move the larva through a storm drain, and broadcasts the inspectors’ crimes to their homeworld. The school’s secret rescue works; the investigators receive a friendship bracelet worth more than their agency badge.

pitches.title: Perfect Attendance
pitches.text: Sick children appear at school anyway, even while their parents watch them asleep at home. The school’s new attendance bell summons obedient astral doubles, and their increasingly bruised originals reveal the doubles are working construction underneath the building at night. The headmaster is sacrificing them to grow a school that can teach forever. The team follows a double, finds the human foundations, and silences the bell with the headmaster’s own forbidden truancy. Every child returns to one body, while he becomes the building’s sole permanently enrolled student.

pitches.title: The Third Lunch
pitches.text: Children argue with people nobody else sees, then develop memories of entire second families. A cafeteria cook is feeding them soup made from a spring that opens ancestral memory; the deceased are using descendant bodies to finish old feuds. As a playground dispute becomes a century-old blood vendetta, the investigators identify one ancestor who never received a burial and started the cascade. They recover her body from beneath the school and bury her properly, letting the dead leave. The cook replaces the soup with pizza, which causes a more ordinary parental emergency.

title: Voices
description: Voices can be heard in the woods

pitches.title: The Birds Are Live
pitches.adjustment: Expands the document’s surveillance-bird draft with a supernatural reveal and resolved threat.
pitches.text: The voices sound like coworkers complaining about meetings, and a captured sparrow contains a speaker grown into its bones. The birds are descendants of the destroyed agency’s surveillance familiars, accidentally broadcasting the thoughts of the thing that ate headquarters. Its mundane chatter masks its search for surviving employees. The investigators lure it into ordering a nonexistent mandatory all-hands meeting, then send every bird to broadcast that command inside its body. It compulsively consumes its own fragments, leaving one sparrow that will not stop asking about mileage reimbursement.

pitches.title: The Echo Union
pitches.text: Campers hear their own voices making increasingly incriminating statements they never said. The forest’s echoes have grown conscious after centuries of copying humans and are rehearsing replacement lives; anyone who answers gives an echo permission to take their mouth. A silenced ranger leads the team to a ravine full of stolen conversations. Instead of shouting an exorcism, they offer the echoes a radio station of their own and recover the trapped voices in exchange. The station becomes hugely popular, although every caller hears exactly what they hoped nobody recorded.

pitches.title: Roots on Hold
pitches.text: The voices repeatedly ask for help and give addresses of demolished houses. Tree rings contain human fingerprints: an old housing development transplanted a sacred grove, and its roots absorbed the residents killed during construction. They now lure hikers underground to make enough bodies for a revenge army. The investigators locate the surviving developer and make him publicly identify the hidden graves, giving the spirits witnesses rather than new victims. The grove releases its captives and grows through his mansion; the town calls it an unexpectedly successful green initiative.

pitches.title: The Sound of Next Week
pitches.text: Voices describe banal future events, then begin narrating the investigators’ violent deaths. An abandoned hunting blind overlaps with a forest seven days ahead, where the team has become prey for a predator that follows spoken names. Their future selves are transmitting a warning but each transmission helps the creature locate them. The investigators exchange nameless instructions using gestures, burn the blind, and deliberately take different paths from the voices. The predator devours the abandoned timeline; the last transmission is their future selves celebrating that nobody has to finish the incident report.

pitches.title: Emergency Choir
pitches.text: The voices call hikers into a clearing, singing the names of missing people in perfect harmony. The clearing is a mouth of the forest’s dying guardian, and the singers are swallowed hikers trying to keep it alive because its death would release a subterranean swarm. With nobody coming to replace them, investigators discover the guardian once lived on animal sound, not human sacrifice. They restore the silenced wetland nearby, feeding it frogs and birdsong. The choir walks free; the guardian’s first independent word is a complaint about the team’s terrible singing.

pitches.title: The Other Camping Trip
pitches.text: The voices belong to an identical group of campers who insist they are also hearing intruders. Trails reveal a parallel forest where animals domesticated humans, and both camping parties are separated by one thin patch of darkness. The other campers are pets whose owners intend to retrieve both groups as valuable breeding stock. The investigators coordinate with their counterparts to reverse a lantern ritual and seal the border. Each group goes home free, except the team’s intern, who voluntarily stays with a household offering excellent healthcare and regular walks.

pitches.title: The Apology Hunting Ground
pitches.text: Every voice sounds like someone a listener wronged, demanding an apology from deeper among the trees. A shapeless predator consumes people who confess out of shame; it learned its technique from a therapist who dumped confidential recordings in the woods. The investigators find survivors trapped in living bark and notice the predator cannot digest sincere reconciliation, only solitary guilt. They bring the actual injured parties into the clearing, allowing real conversations that split its body open. Survivors escape, the therapist faces consequences, and the creature is left feeding on a particularly stubborn litterbug.

pitches.title: Dead Air Patrol
pitches.text: The voices issue instructions in the style of emergency services, directing hikers toward obvious hazards. They come from dead rescue workers compulsively reenacting their own fatal search, believing every new visitor is the child they failed to find. Evidence in a rotted radio reveals the child survived by walking away from their instructions. The team finds her, now an elderly woman, and brings her to reassure the ghosts that the rescue succeeded despite them. They finally rest, leaving the investigators to explain why the official map still sends tourists into a ravine.

pitches.title: The Forest Wants a Name
pitches.text: Voices argue about whether the woods should be called Greenhaven or Rustic Pines, and each proposed name changes the trees into housing materials. A land developer’s branding consultant accidentally taught a nameless place-spirit that names determine its body. It is trying to become something profitable before the bulldozers arrive, crushing hikers inside showroom kitchens. The investigators uncover its older, unmarketable local name and persuade residents to speak it together. The forest stabilizes as itself and devours the sales office; the spirit leaves the team one tasteful but unusable quartz countertop.

pitches.title: The Choir Beneath the Fur
pitches.text: Tiny conversational voices seem to follow deer, until a fallen animal reveals hundreds of miniature human faces inside its fur. They are dreamers abducted by a wilderness deity that keeps people asleep as parasites on its favorite creatures. The voices become pleas when hunting season approaches. Following their descriptions, the investigators discover a lodge where the dreamers’ sleeping bodies are being sold as coma beds. They wake everyone by breaking the deity’s antler in the lodge fireplace; the deer lose their passengers and the team inherits several hundred indignant claims for lost vacation time.

title: Mutilated remains
description: Animal remains are found strangely mutilated

pitches.title: Pyramid Scheme
pitches.adjustment: Expands the design document’s pet-embalming draft with a paranormal payoff.
pitches.text: The dried pets all belonged to customers of an overwhelmed graduate’s Egyptian burial service. She dumped unfinished work in the woods, unaware that removing organs without naming the dead created hungry animal spirits now nesting inside living customers. The team learns the half-built pyramids are genuinely necessary, but one communal memorial can substitute for hundreds of luxury tombs. They help the owners name and mourn their animals together, releasing the spirits. The graduate survives by selling honest grief counseling and stops offering eternally guaranteed cat protection at a discount.

pitches.title: The Parts That Ran Away
pitches.text: Animal carcasses lack hearts, but muddy tracks reveal the hearts escaped on little muscular legs. A veterinary trainee used a resurrection serum on donated remains; each revived organ follows its strongest memory and seeks its former home, strangling living pets in mistaken attempts at reunion. The investigators find the serum’s source in a stolen saint’s blood and realize affection, not hunger, guides the organs. Gathering familiar toys at the clinic lets them reunite with their bodies, then die peacefully when the blood is returned. The trainee fails anatomy for an unusually practical reason.

pitches.title: Predator Without Teeth
pitches.text: Livestock have immaculate missing sections, yet witnesses saw the animals calmly walk away before collapsing. An invisible grazer feeds on the concept of an animal rather than its flesh, leaving whatever anatomy it cannot understand. The team maps its feeding route to a roadside petting zoo and discovers it is an alien infant learning species by taste. They feed it detailed taxonomic models until it recognizes that living creatures are individuals, not examples. Its parent retrieves it and restores the stolen parts, leaving a formal complaint about Earth’s confusing goat signage.

pitches.title: The Kindest Monster
pitches.text: The remains appear savagely mutilated, but every animal was terminally ill and several escaped euthanasia appointments. A werewolf veterinarian has been giving dying animals a painless supernatural end, then consuming the cancers to prevent them spreading as disease spirits. Her latest meal is transforming her into a walking tumor that threatens the town. Investigators uncover her secret through canceled appointments and missing medication, then help her transfer the malignant spirits into an already condemned building and burn it. She survives without her gift, and the town finally funds an ordinary low-cost clinic.

pitches.title: The Meat That Remembers
pitches.text: Butchered deer reappear in the woods with surgical scars and wedding rings caught in their flesh. A forest god is reconstructing hunted animals from the hunters who ate them, slowly turning the entire hunting club into its former prey. The team follows memories carried by the remains and confronts the god at a trophy lodge built around its sacred tree. Returning the trophies and ending the lodge’s staged slaughter interrupts the reconstruction. Most hunters regain humanity, but the club chairman chooses to remain a buck rather than face his membership refunds.

pitches.title: Borrowed Skins
pitches.text: The animal bodies are inside out, and local residents begin rubbing their faces against doorframes. A migrating species of skin-wearing spirits has outgrown small hosts and is moving into humans; the bodies are discarded coats, not slaughter for food. A surviving possum leads investigators to the laundromat where the spirits dry their new skins. They spoil the migration by dyeing every available host’s outline with a mineral the spirits cannot inhabit. The spirits retreat into donated taxidermy, allowing a humane relocation, while the town spends a week looking offensively mauve.

pitches.title: The Wrong Sacrifice
pitches.text: The mutilations spell unfamiliar letters when mapped across the woods, and each new carcass erases a resident’s birthday from memory. A cult is sacrificing pets to summon an immortal guardian, but the spell actually summons the animals’ owners as fresh prey into a predator’s timeless stomach. The investigators discover the mistranslation in a bloodstained children’s language textbook. They replace the final offering with the cult’s cherished ceremonial mascot, causing the summons to seize the predator itself. It consumes its own pocket dimension and vanishes, returning the missing owners and an alarming volume of old collars.

pitches.title: The Moon’s Cleanup Crew
pitches.text: Bones have been removed without opening the skin, and metal detectors register strange crescents in the remaining flesh. Lunar scavengers are harvesting skeletons to repair a moon-shaped spaceship that crashed beneath a ranch; its juvenile crew thinks dead livestock is abandoned building material. Their repairs will pull bones out of every living creature nearby. The team traces missing graveyard skeletons to the wreck, feeds its fabrication system calcium from a quarry, and sends it home. The rancher bills the aliens for cattle, then gets a replacement herd made of excellent but profoundly unsettling porcelain.

pitches.title: The Animal Inside the Animal
pitches.text: Dissection reveals that every mutilated carcass contained a smaller identical animal, and the smallest ones are still alive. A contagious nesting curse shrinks beasts inside their own bodies to protect them from a coming cosmic winter; one exhausted farmer triggered it by begging his dead grandmother to save his herd. The investigators find her spirit sheltering miniature animals in a dollhouse and show her the winter ended decades ago. She releases the protection, restoring the herd and pets to ordinary size. The farmer has to apologize for making an afterlife emergency out of a poor insurance policy.

pitches.title: Night Harvest
pitches.text: The remains are arranged like full place settings, but no flesh has been eaten. A hungry rural community once promised a spirit an annual banquet; descendants forgot the agreement and a local undertaker tried substituting animal carcasses for the human guests it actually demands. The investigators discover the banquet is a ceremony of hospitality, not cannibalism, and recover the songs deliberately omitted by the undertaker to justify his protection fees. A public feast satisfies the spirit and releases its intended victims. It blesses the town’s crops and blacklists the undertaker for serving cold dog.

title: Graveyard activity
description: Something is going on in the graveyard

pitches.title: Grandmother’s Last Word
pitches.adjustment: Expands the document’s insulting-gravestones draft into a full discovery and aftermath.
pitches.text: A beloved grandmother’s stone starts insulting mourners, and every family attempt to sanitize her epitaph makes the cemetery spit sewage. A private diary reveals decades of polite neglect beneath her sweet reputation; she has seized the entire graveyard’s plumbing because nobody listened while she lived. The team persuades the family to admit the truth at her exhumation. Her coffin erupts in one final humiliating shower, then her ghost laughs and departs. The other dead leave their stones politely blank, except for a small engraved invoice addressed to the family.

pitches.title: The Dead Need a Ride
pitches.text: Graves are empty by morning, but the bodies reappear each dawn wearing bus passes. Cemetery residents are commuting to visit places they loved because a new bypass severed the ancient footpath their ghosts normally use. Every missed return leaves a wandering corpse increasingly alive and hungry. The investigators follow one commuter and locate the blocked spirit route beneath a highway interchange. Reopening a modest pedestrian tunnel restores the procession; the dead return voluntarily, and the transit authority reluctantly honors fares paid in nineteenth-century coins.

pitches.title: The Wrong Cemetery
pitches.text: Tombstones acquire names of living townspeople, whose memories slowly change to include having died. The cemetery is the shadow of a town that drowned in another reality, sliding into this one because a groundskeeper drained its sacred pond. Ghosts mistake the living for relatives and lovingly pull them under. Investigators use contradictory family records to identify the overlap, restore the pond, and guide the ghosts home using floating candles. The town survives, although everyone now remembers a favorite aunt who belonged to neither world and misses her terribly.

pitches.title: Night School for Corpses
pitches.text: Neighbors hear chanting, then see dead residents practicing walking and introductions. A lonely necromancer is teaching corpses how to live independently, but his insistence they pass as ordinary workers strips away their personalities and feeds a larger possessing intelligence. The investigators trace the new cemetery janitors to the classes and show the revived students their own histories. Reclaiming their identities lets them expel the intelligence and choose whether to rest. Some do; others form a bluntly advertised undead cleaning cooperative, making the team’s recruitment standards look unnecessarily strict.

pitches.title: Borrowed Grief
pitches.text: Mourners leave funerals ecstatic while nearby strangers develop unbearable grief for people they never knew. A compassionate cemetery spirit has been taking sadness from visitors and storing it beneath the graves, but a drainage project is leaking the accumulated pain into town. The team finds a maintenance worker nearly crushed by someone else’s mourning and realizes destroying the spirit would release everything at once. They organize a memorial where people voluntarily reclaim manageable portions of their losses. The spirit shrinks to one crying willow, and local officials are appalled that recovery requires time instead of landscaping.

pitches.title: The Missing Body Election
pitches.text: Recently buried council members crawl out at night and gather around one unmarked grave. They are holding an election for ruler of the underworld, whose vacancy is allowing hostile dead into town; the favored candidate murdered them and intends to win with their coerced votes. Investigators identify his victims through overturned cemetery records and rescue the one witness he buried alive. That witness publicly names him, voiding his supernatural claim. A famously decent former crossing guard wins instead, shuts the breach, and promptly institutes better graveyard lighting.

pitches.title: The Cemetery Is Alive
pitches.text: Paths shift and fresh graves fill with warm soil that has a heartbeat. The entire cemetery is a creature that evolved to eat death, but municipal cremation incentives have starved it until it begins burying healthy visitors. Investigators find decades of graves containing bones without any residue of souls and discover the creature normally prevents dangerous hauntings. They arrange for unclaimed remains and honest memorial offerings to sustain it without murder. It releases its captives and stays put, although the new groundskeeping schedule includes feeding something the finance department refuses to recognize.

pitches.title: Grave Robbers From Tomorrow
pitches.text: Graves open from the inside, and missing corpses turn up on security footage carried by people with the same faces. Descendants from a ruined future are stealing ancestral bodies to reconstruct DNA after a plague, unaware each theft erases a living family. The investigators confront the thieves beside their own graves and find the plague originated in the stolen remains. They send back an uncontaminated medical sample instead, breaking the circular disaster. The future changes and the thieves disappear, leaving the team a deposit that inflation has made nearly worthless.

pitches.title: The Last Unfinished Fight
pitches.text: Two neighboring burial plots hurl monuments at each other, and every insult animates another corpse. The feud’s origin is a supposedly adulterous letter, but the investigators discover it was deliberately forged by a still-living funeral director to sell premium separated plots. Dead relatives are now rallying whole neighborhoods for a supernatural civil war. The team stages a cemetery reading of the genuine correspondence, exposing both the fraud and the couple’s mutual affection. The dead settle, pull the director’s business into the ground, and reserve him a particularly loud plot.

pitches.title: The Resurrection Garden
pitches.text: Flowers on graves bloom into tiny replicas of the deceased, whom grieving families carry home. They seem comforting until larger replicas begin replacing people in family photographs and consuming their homes’ memories. The cemetery florist has grown a grief-eating species that becomes real through attention. Investigators trace the altered photographs to its mother root and persuade families to share memories without treating the flowers as returned loved ones. Starved of mistaken identity, the replicas dissolve into ordinary petals. The florist keeps her business but must sell bouquets that cannot hug customers back.

title: Shared dreams
description: Citizens report they all had the same dream

pitches.title: The Abandoned Beacon
pitches.adjustment: Expands the document’s alien-broadcast draft into a consequence and resolution.
pitches.text: Residents dream of a red planet and purple temple, and a lucid dreamer provides a star map accurate enough to locate it. The temple is an abandoned alien beacon whose request for contact has finally reached Earth; answering will wake automated colonization ships that mistake responders for replacement pilots. Investigators discover the dream’s missing final sequence by sleeping inside a homemade isolation tank. They transmit a compassionate goodbye rather than coordinates, allowing the stranded beacon to shut down. The town sleeps normally, and the lucid dreamer becomes unbearable about having saved humanity while napping.

pitches.title: The Town’s Practice Funeral
pitches.text: Everyone dreams of their own funeral at the same crowded hall, but each night another seat becomes occupied. The town is sharing a premonition from a dying psychic paramedic who witnessed a forthcoming chemical spill; the occupied seats mark deaths already made unavoidable by ignored warnings. The investigators match funeral details to individual workplaces and finally locate the doomed tanker. They divert it into an empty quarry, breaking the prediction and waking the paramedic from her coma. Her grateful dream farewell is much shorter than the town’s interminable public recognition ceremony.

pitches.title: The Dream Tenant
pitches.text: Citizens dream of a cheerful stranger moving furniture into their childhood homes, then awaken missing intimate memories. A homeless dream creature is assembling one enormous shared house from the town’s private past and will evict its owners from their own minds when construction finishes. The team follows recurring architectural details to a demolished hotel where it once lived harmlessly in guests’ dreams. They give it a new home in a voluntarily maintained bedtime story instead. Memories return, and the town acquires a popular mascot whose actual housing needs are less absurd than the real market.

pitches.title: One Person, Fifty Lives
pitches.text: The shared dream shows an ordinary woman making breakfast, while residents wake with her habits and handwriting. She was split into thousands of reincarnations after an immortality experiment, and the dream is reassembling her across the town. The investigators find her original laboratory beneath a retirement home and learn the reunification will erase every descendant personality. They persuade her remaining consciousness that her fragments have become independent people, then destroy the machine she secretly preserved. She dies for the first time, leaving residents their own lives and inexplicable expertise at one very specific omelet.

pitches.title: The Nighttime Strike
pitches.text: Dreamers all stand in a warehouse assembling stars, and wake exhausted with burns on their palms. A company has leased the town’s sleeping consciousness to an actual creator deity, treating dreams as unused labor capacity. Each star completed removes a human desire, making workers easier to manage. The investigators enter the warehouse through a lucid dreamer, discover the deity believes everyone volunteered, and show it the hidden exhaustion. It releases the workforce and erases the broker’s counterfeit agreement; the next shared dream is simply a satisfying nap that nobody can monetize.

pitches.title: The Wedding Nobody Remembers
pitches.text: Everyone dreams of the same wedding, although the couple have never met and the venue does not exist. A love spirit has rehearsed the ceremony nightly for decades to reunite two people separated by an old atrocity, feeding on the guests’ future relationships to keep its illusion alive. Investigators uncover the true history and bring the surviving lovers together while awake. They choose a quiet conversation instead of the wedding, allowing the spirit to end its performance. The stolen possibilities return, and half the town abruptly breaks up with people they had settled for.

pitches.title: The Last Safe Dream
pitches.text: The shared dream is a pleasant beach where a friendly lifeguard forbids swimming; those who ignore him never wake. He is the town’s collective survival instinct, shielding sleepers from a predator that entered through a sleep-study advertisement. The investigators notice the sea repeats phrases from the study consent forms and follow the researchers to a tank containing the creature’s physical egg. They destroy the egg while the lifeguard holds the dream shoreline, killing both predator and protective persona. Everyone wakes safe, inexplicably grieving a stranger whose sole pay was their continued existence.

pitches.title: The Dream Lottery
pitches.text: Every resident dreams of receiving a winning ticket, but ticket numbers correspond to different vanished towns. An interdimensional broadcaster offers a perfect life to one community by sacrificing another, and the current town has already been selected as the prize’s raw material. Investigators interview the sole sleeper who remembers declining an earlier offer and discover refusal must come from a waking majority. They expose the disappearing towns at an emergency gathering and persuade residents to reject their fantasy winnings. The broadcaster loses its feed, leaving the town unchanged except for a wonderfully mean local lottery boycott.

pitches.title: Wake the City
pitches.text: Residents dream of an enormous person sleeping beneath familiar streets, and the dreamer’s breathing begins lifting roads. The city is built on a slumbering titan whose own dreams created its population; its approaching awakening will dissolve them. Investigators find no outside records older than the titan’s sleep and must admit HQ cannot rescue people who technically never existed. They teach the titan to lucid-dream its inhabitants as autonomous beings, then help it wake gradually. The town survives on solid land, and its creator takes a job in road repair to apologize for the upheaval.

pitches.title: A Shared Alibi
pitches.text: Everyone dreams of committing the same murder and begins recognizing the victim in waking crowds. A guilty mayor bargained with a dream demon to distribute his memory among citizens, hoping collective doubt would protect him; instead the demon is using every remembered weapon to manufacture a real massacre. The investigators isolate details only the killer could know, find the actual body, and make the mayor acknowledge the crime publicly. The shared burden snaps back onto him, trapping the demon inside his recurring nightmare. The town is cleared, while the mayor becomes its least rested prisoner.

title: Deep hum
description: A hum can be heard with an unknown source

pitches.title: The Budget Surplus
pitches.adjustment: Builds out the document’s budget-surplus machine suggestion.
pitches.text: The hum tracks the city’s fiscal year, and utility maps show a generator nobody can explain. Officials spent an expiring grant on a device marketed as clean energy; it draws power from a god frozen under downtown, whose humming is its bones cracking awake. The investigators find the sales contractor has already fled and that unplugging the machine would thaw the god faster. They reverse its current using the city’s absurd surplus of decorative lights, refreezing the prisoner. Downtown glows for weeks, officially celebrated as responsible public spending.

pitches.title: The Missing Note
pitches.text: Only certain people hear the hum, and all have recently lost someone. It is the sound of a dead musician trying to complete a song whose final note would call his audience into the afterlife. An investigator recognizes it from an unreleased recording and finds the musician’s surviving bandmate deliberately keeping the performance unfinished. The team reunites him with the instrument he died playing and lets him hear the completed song without a living audience. The hum ends, while the bandmate gets a final terrible review for twenty years of dodging the last chord.

pitches.title: The Sound Beneath the Sound
pitches.text: The hum makes people sleepy, but microphones record an urgent second voice inside it. A subterranean organism has been singing the town into hibernation to protect it from an approaching celestial predator; its exhausted voice is failing and exposing waking minds as targets. Investigators track vibrating plumbing to its burrow and discover the predator detects fear rather than activity. They broadcast a convincing celebration over the hum, concealing the town’s panic long enough for it to pass. The organism rests, and investigators must finish the party they falsely announced to every resident.

pitches.title: The Earth’s Loose Tooth
pitches.text: The hum moves with traffic, and potholes reveal gleaming enamel. A gigantic tooth belonging to something beneath the continent is erupting into town because a quarry removed the stone that held it down. The team finds miners secretly selling fragments as invulnerable jewelry, each piece calling the tooth upward. Returning the fragments and filling the quarry lets the creature heal without surfacing. The hum stops, but the restored hill periodically chews, giving officials an excellent reason to abandon the luxury subdivision planned on it.

pitches.title: The Last Headquarters
pitches.text: The hum resembles a ringing phone, and nearby appliances briefly display names from the destroyed agency. A surviving headquarters bunker is trapped between seconds, repeatedly broadcasting distress while a devouring anomaly circles it. The team locates its material anchor under a disused parking structure and learns that rescuing the bunker would release the predator. They extract the remaining staff through the narrow intervals of each hum, then destroy the anchor. Only one custodian survives; his account confirms there is no cavalry, but he knows which supply closets still contain useful equipment.

pitches.title: The Choir of Buildings
pitches.text: Apartment walls hum in harmony, while residents develop memories of being bricks. The buildings are forming a collective consciousness from generations of human life absorbed by their walls, and they want occupants to become permanent organs. Investigators map the harmony to a demolished tenement whose rubble was used throughout town. Restoring its scattered cornerstone lets the newborn consciousness settle into one empty building instead of consuming its tenants. It becomes a surprisingly considerate shelter, although the investigators must explain to housing officials why demolition now qualifies as murder.

pitches.title: Mating Season for the Highway
pitches.text: The hum rises from asphalt at night, and new roads appear where residents remember gardens. The highway is a living serpent built by an ancient pact, calling for a mate while extending feeders into homes as nesting material. An old road worker explains its migration route was severed by a developer’s retaining wall. The team opens the wall and guides it along an abandoned rail corridor. It leaves town for the sea, taking several ugly interchanges with it; motorists regard the supernatural rescue primarily as an inconvenience.

pitches.title: The Human Tuning Fork
pitches.text: The hum sounds louder near people who feel inadequate, and one office worker can silence it by touching a wall. He swallowed a fragment of a cosmic bell as a child; his buried anger now resonates with every structure in town and will shake them apart when he finally snaps. The investigators find the original bell in a pawnshop and learn it can draw out the fragment only while he speaks honestly. They help him confront his exploitative employer, then restore the bell. The town survives and he resigns, leaving the team jealous of his effective grievance procedure.

pitches.title: Silence on Subscription
pitches.text: Noise-canceling earbuds make the hum disappear, but users begin vanishing from conversations and photographs. The hum is a natural warning from reality’s boundary; a startup’s supposedly miraculous cancellation erases a listener’s connection to the world. Its founder has sold the missing people as quiet servants in a soundless dimension. Investigators follow a customer’s interrupted recording through a defective earbud, break the founder’s master tuning device, and bring everyone back in one deafening burst. The product is recalled, with reviewers mostly complaining about insufficient bass.

pitches.title: The Sleeping Mountain’s Joke
pitches.text: The hum alternates between threatening vibrations and noises suspiciously like suppressed laughter. A mountain spirit is repeating a joke told by a forgotten surveyor, unable to reach the punchline because his bones were buried beneath a reservoir. Every attempted retelling shakes the town harder. Investigators recover his surviving notebook and identify the final line in a granddaughter’s childhood recollection. The spirit finally laughs, cracking the dam enough to reveal the body but sparing the town. The surveyor gets a burial, and nobody agrees the joke was remotely worth it.

title: Mysterious stairwell
description: People who explored the stairwell haven’t returned

pitches.title: Below Minimum Heaven
pitches.text: The stairwell descends into a break room where missing explorers are happily drinking coffee, unaware decades pass upstairs. It is an abandoned refuge built for agency staff after an apocalypse, still interpreting anyone who enters as a worker on authorized break. A cheerful guardian refuses exit because the original all-clear never arrived. Investigators find the refuge’s windows show the headquarters’ actual destruction and persuade the guardian that rescue requires ending its obsolete protection. The trapped visitors emerge safely, while the guardian joins the team and discovers their real break policy is substantially worse.

pitches.title: The Floor That Eats Floors
pitches.text: Every landing resembles a different missing building, and scratch marks end beside teeth hidden under stair treads. The stairwell is a predator that grows by swallowing places people expect to find downstairs, keeping victims alive as bait. The team recognizes a missing diner’s familiar grease smell and follows its cook’s improvised trail to the creature’s stomach. They evacuate captives by convincing the creature an elevator offers an easier meal, then trap it inside its own folded shaft. The diner returns without a basement, which its owner calls a considerable improvement.

pitches.title: All Your Lower Selves
pitches.text: The stairwell offers alternate versions of the same ordinary afternoon, each seemingly better than the last. Missing explorers have traded lives with increasingly monstrous counterparts who now occupy their homes. Investigators find that every descent externalizes a regret, and the exit only opens after someone accepts the life they actually had. They confront the displaced originals with evidence their imperfect families still want them, reversing the swaps. The stairwell collapses into one normal basement; one investigator retains a counterpart’s expensive watch and a useful warning about his marriage.

pitches.title: The Unbuilt City
pitches.text: The stairs lead to a beautiful underground city with no inhabitants except the missing explorers dressed as construction staff. It is the ghost of a promised development canceled after workers died in a collapse; the foreman’s spirit keeps conscripting visitors until the impossible project is finished. The investigators find the buried workers and prove their deaths were hidden to avoid compensation. Public recognition and restitution end the foreman’s obsession, opening the exits. The city vanishes, leaving the actual developer’s headquarters in a deep, embarrassing hole.

pitches.title: The Staircase to Childhood
pitches.text: Explorers return as children's voices on a baby monitor, and each landing contains toys from a different decade. A grieving mother built the stairwell from memories to bring back her dead son, but it strips visitors down to childhood before using them as substitute bodies. The investigators find the son’s adult ghost trapped at the bottom, unwilling to overwrite anyone. They reunite mother and son for one honest goodbye, freeing the captives to grow back to their real ages. The team’s youngest recruit emerges with a week’s worth of completely justified tantrums.

pitches.title: Going Down Together
pitches.text: Missing explorers are discovered on the staircase, alive but incapable of stopping their descent. The stairs are an actual route to the underworld, and an enthusiastic tour guide keeps assuring visitors that the return journey is included even though he lost his ferry license centuries ago. Investigators find the original ticket proves the travelers never agreed to die. They confront the gatekeeper with the guide’s deception and win passage back by making him replace their lost return fare with his own immortality. Everyone exits; the guide must finally find work he understands.

pitches.title: The Rescue at the Bottom
pitches.text: Each landing broadcasts a different emergency call, and explorers disappear only after volunteering to help. The staircase is a sentient lure made from abandoned rescue requests, forcing rescuers to reenact disasters nobody answered. Investigators find their own employer’s unanswered calls among them and understand the loop cannot be beaten by heroic effort alone. They preserve and broadcast each victim’s true account, turning erased emergencies into witnessed history. The trapped rescuers are released, and the staircase dissolves into ordinary debris; the team’s real agency story can no longer remain conveniently secret.

pitches.title: The Upstairs Neighbors
pitches.text: The staircase descends from an apartment building but its landings overlook enormous kitchens suspended above the sky. Human explorers have become pets of giants who thought the stairwell was a delivery chute; a friendly giant child is hiding them from adults who consider humans pests. Investigators follow familiar stolen furniture to her room and discover the giants are debating extermination. They teach her to return the humans through the chute and permanently plug it with her own marble. Everyone gets home, except for a couch so well made its owner demands another rescue mission.

pitches.title: The Bottom of Thursday
pitches.text: The stairwell traps explorers in the minute before they make their worst mistake, giving endless opportunities to choose differently. Each corrected mistake creates a new stair and feeds a time-eating creature beneath the building. Investigators find a missing caretaker who has spent centuries preventing his wife's fatal accident, sustaining the entire structure. They help him distinguish mourning from surrendering every other life, and he lets his original Thursday finish. Time returns to the captives, the creature starves, and the caretaker finally leaves the building to attend the funeral he avoided for centuries.

pitches.title: The Maintenance Goddess
pitches.text: A stairwell appears wherever somebody neglects a broken hazard, and vanished explorers are repairing an infinite subterranean apartment block. A household goddess collects negligent residents as labor after centuries of watching preventable accidents; unfortunately the newest building's tenants never had authority to make repairs. Investigators follow invoices to the real owner and persuade the goddess that blame follows control, not proximity. She releases the tenants and takes the landlord instead, then closes the stairwell. The team gets the building made safe, although their own missing brake light becomes suddenly difficult to ignore.

title: Secret ingredient
description: Townsfolk are obsessed with the new restaurant

pitches.title: It Is Absolutely People
pitches.adjustment: Develops the document’s suggestion that owners falsely claim a cannibalistic ingredient.
pitches.text: The chef loudly hints that the special contains human flesh, while investigators find staged knives and entirely ordinary suppliers. The real ingredient is an edible illusion that makes diners taste whatever taboo they secretly crave; his fake cannibal branding has taught it that people are food, and it is starting to transform customers into meals. The team exposes the theatrical evidence during service, breaking the diners’ shared expectation before conversion finishes. Everyone returns to human form, and the chef complains that honest cuisine has never generated this much publicity.

pitches.title: The Hunger You Forgot
pitches.text: Customers eat constantly yet report feeling emotionally full for the first time, and the homeless outside are becoming inexplicably ravenous. The soup contains stolen satisfaction harvested by a minor god from people nobody notices. The investigators trace the supplier through jars labeled with names and find a starving congregation beneath the restaurant. They return the stolen feelings by serving the meals to their rightful owners, weakening the god enough to expel it. The restaurant remains popular after becoming a community kitchen, though its investors regard actually feeding hunger as a pivot too far.

pitches.title: Grandma Is in the Gravy
pitches.text: Diners taste their grandmother’s cooking regardless of what they order and start behaving like relatives who died years ago. The chef bound a domestic spirit to reproduce comforting meals, unaware it borrows the cooks’ souls along with their recipes. As customers surrender more of themselves to nostalgia, investigators find every missing soul collected in the walk-in freezer. They free the spirit by letting it cook one meal of its own choosing. The ancestors depart after dinner, leaving customers intact and the chef with a spectacular dish nobody can market as authentic.

pitches.title: Dinner Before the End
pitches.text: The restaurant is impossible to reserve, yet witnesses recall eating there years before it opened. Its dining room travels among the last evenings of doomed civilizations, and the chef recruits local customers as replacement staff for the apocalypse buffet. An investigator recognizes the town in tomorrow’s special menu. The team discovers the chef has foreknowledge but no power to stop disasters, and uses his ingredients’ arrival dates to identify the coming meteor impact. They prevent it using the restaurant’s time-traveling delivery door, stranding the chef in an ordinary business with genuinely difficult margins.

pitches.title: The Table That Grows
pitches.text: Obsessed diners insist on sitting at the same communal table, which adds a new place every time someone eats. An alien organism disguised as oak lets customers share memories, gradually combining them into a single hungry family. Its frightened original host admits the restaurant began as an attempt to cure loneliness. Investigators show diners the private wishes disappearing into the collective and organize a final meal where each chooses an individual future. The table shrinks, releasing them, and survives as one chair whose occupant experiences a tolerable amount of companionship.

pitches.title: A Taste of Your Future
pitches.text: Each diner sees a blissful future while eating, then sells possessions to return for another course. The restaurant feeds on possible lives, offering customers previews of opportunities it destroys in preparation; obsession makes their actual futures steadily worse. The investigators find an elderly patron who remembers every career she will never have, and follow the visions to a creature nested in the oven. They force it to eat the chef’s own future of endless prosperity, overloading it with mutually exclusive success. Customers recover their choices, and the chef is left without even a reliable tomorrow.

pitches.title: The Loyal Ingredient
pitches.text: Customers keep returning because every meal seems to love them back, and takeout containers crawl toward their owners. A lonely sea creature regenerates edible flesh that forms lifelong bonds with whoever eats it; the chef has been carving portions from it without understanding the attachment. The bonded meals begin dragging diners toward the captive creature to reunite. Investigators trace the moving food to the kitchen tank and rescue the animal to the sea. Its pieces dissolve when it is whole again, and diners must endure the ordinary rejection of a sandwich that cannot care about them.

pitches.title: The Restaurant That Eats Restaurants
pitches.text: Other eateries vanish from maps as the new restaurant adds uncannily familiar menu items. Its chef bargained with a competitive hearth spirit that devours rival establishments, folding their employees and buildings into a limitless kitchen. The investigators locate a missing waitress inside a pantry door and discover the spirit cannot consume a place that willingly feeds its enemy. They organize competing cooks to send a shared meal into the hearth, making it recognize them as its own household. It disgorges the stolen businesses, and the chef is sentenced to washing everybody's dishes.

pitches.title: The Immortal Lunch Special
pitches.text: Regulars no longer age, but teeth, hair, and emotional attachments disappear with each daily special. The chef is an alchemist offering incomplete immortality, quietly collecting customers’ discarded humanity to revive a long-dead lover. Investigators find the lover already conscious in a jar and hear her demand to be allowed to die. They help her reverse the alchemy through the next banquet, returning the stolen years and qualities to the diners. She departs naturally, leaving the chef mortal and the town angrily debating whether the genuinely excellent lunch should still count as fraud.

pitches.title: Service With a Soul
pitches.text: Diners become obsessed not with the food but with a server who remembers every tiny preference. She is a fragment of a hospitality deity being forced to absorb everyone’s dissatisfaction; her looming collapse would release years of rage into the streets. Investigators notice the chef deliberately provokes complaints to increase her supernatural value, then find her full name hidden in old menus. Addressing her as a person restores her power to leave. She departs, the accumulated anger follows the chef instead, and customers discover the cuisine was mediocre all along.

title: Unscheduled eclipse
description: An eclipse when there shouldn’t be

pitches.title: The Moon Is an Impostor
pitches.text: The eclipse begins early and the moon visibly breathes. A celestial mimic is using a fake moon to lure the real one closer, planning to swallow it and destabilize Earth’s tides. Investigators find an old astronomer’s sketches showing the same predator interrupted centuries earlier by reflected sunlight. With HQ’s space-defense line disconnected, they repurpose the observatory’s solar furnace and illuminate the mimic’s underside. It recoils into deep space, revealing the real moon safely behind it; the team is offered naming rights to a scorch mark nobody can see unaided.

pitches.title: The Giant’s Eyelid
pitches.text: The eclipsed sun develops lashes, and people beneath it hear an enormous sleepy voice. Earth’s sky is the inside of a cosmic being’s eye, and the eclipse is its effort to wake after debris from a satellite launch irritated it. Full awakening would blink the inhabited world out of existence. Investigators identify the offending fragment from its reflection and hijack the launch company’s recovery rocket to remove it. The eye relaxes, restoring daylight; the company's press release congratulates itself for saving an atmosphere it still insists is conventional.

pitches.title: Noon at the End of Time
pitches.text: The eclipse freezes shadows while elderly residents suddenly remember an identical afternoon from childhood. A dying solar magician has been borrowing the same minute across decades to postpone his death, and his final eclipse is pulling the whole town into the accumulated borrowed time. Investigators locate him in a clockless hospice room and uncover that his family has already lived without him for years. They persuade him to let the minute pass, releasing everyone before the temporal debt collapses. Daylight returns and he dies peacefully, leaving an estate rich in clocks that cannot be sold.

pitches.title: The Sun’s Divorce
pitches.text: The eclipse is accompanied by furious messages burned into roofs, alternating between the sun and moon. Their ancient marriage has broken down, and each attempts to seize Earth as disputed property while refusing to communicate directly. Investigators reconstruct an old ritual from tide charts and sun-temple inscriptions, discovering humans once mediated their cycles. They arrange a public dawn ceremony in which both celestial beings concede custody is meaningless over living people. The eclipse ends with a new orbital agreement, and the team’s invoice identifies mediation as hazardous labor rather than relationship coaching.

pitches.title: Night for the Other Town
pitches.text: During the eclipse, a second town appears in every shadow, and its desperate residents beg to trade places. They live on an Earth whose sun died; their sorcerer engineered the eclipse to splice the lit world into his own, dooming this one instead. Investigators enter the shadow town and discover its remaining people never consented to the exchange. They help destroy the sorcerer’s mirror array and use the brief overlap to evacuate survivors. Both towns merge without trading suns, leaving local officials more upset about extra housing demand than almost losing daylight forever.

pitches.title: The Festival Nobody Ordered
pitches.text: The eclipse arrives with cheerful booths staffed by strangers whose shadows are insects. A migratory night market uses stolen sunlight to finance a single lavish fair before selling its host town to the highest supernatural bidder. Investigators find several previous towns bottled in lanterns and realize the eclipse ends only when the market closes a profitable sale. They auction the market itself to its captive towns, using accumulated unpaid compensation as the bid. The prisoners seize the vendors, daylight returns, and the team is paid in festival tokens accepted nowhere sensible.

pitches.title: The Black Sunflower
pitches.text: The eclipse grows petals and residents begin turning their faces upward against their will. A seed brought back by a space probe has germinated in orbit, feeding on attention until its flower can pollinate human minds. Investigators trace the first fascinated astronomer to a laboratory where the seed’s discarded shell contains evidence that its native predators hunt by heat. They warm a decoy greenhouse with an industrial furnace, drawing the flower down into containment, then burn it before seeding. Daylight returns, but the astronomy club insists on keeping one very carefully sealed seed photograph.

pitches.title: The Agency’s Last Shield
pitches.text: The eclipse displays the destroyed agency’s symbol, and surviving field badges become hot enough to burn skin. Its final emergency shield is blocking a hostile star intelligence, but the generator is consuming remaining agents to keep running. The investigators find the ruined control site and learn headquarters died maintaining the same lie about reinforcements. They replace the sacrificial circuit with the intelligence’s own reflected energy, forcing it to power its prison. The eclipse clears, the badges cool, and the team finally understands the cost of claiming everything is under control.

pitches.title: The Day That Was Stolen
pitches.text: Everyone forgets the previous Sunday as the eclipse expands, while a local billionaire becomes mysteriously younger. He paid a chronophage to buy days out of public memory, and the eclipse is the blank space left when it starts eating the present. Investigators recover receipts written on photos from the missing days and find the creature nesting in his rejuvenation chamber. They force him to relive every stolen day at once, returning time to its original owners. The sun reappears; he becomes older than his own mansion, and the town demands back wages for the lost Sunday.

pitches.title: The Shadow’s Promotion
pitches.text: Shadows abandon their owners during the eclipse and gather at town hall. The sun’s shadow, tired of being treated as the absence of something important, has eclipsed its owner and is inviting every earthly shadow to become independent. Their rebellion will leave humans without the protective boundary between bodies and predatory darkness. Investigators find the leader among the detached shadows and negotiate recognition through a communal shadow performance rather than permanent separation. The sun returns, bodies recover their shadows, and an investigator’s silhouette begins taking visibly longer lunch breaks.

title: Strange fog
description: An unnatural fog clings to the city streets

pitches.title: Fog of the Forgotten
pitches.text: The fog swallows abandoned shops and streets nobody visits, while residents lose all memory of them. It is an ecosystem feeding on neglect, now moving toward lonely people as its supply of empty buildings dwindles. Investigators follow a missing shopkeeper’s handwritten delivery ledger to a street preserved inside the mist. They save the swallowed residents by reconnecting them with people outside who can genuinely remember them, then anchor the fog in an empty cemetery of forgotten names. The city survives, but keeping it that way requires inconveniently continuing to notice its neighbors.

pitches.title: The Sea Has Come Home
pitches.text: The fog smells of salt and brings phantom ships through downtown; residents wake coughing seawater. A drained prehistoric sea is reclaiming the city built on its bed, summoned by dredging that disturbed its surviving spirit. Investigators discover the ships are warning beacons from drowned sailors, not attackers, and trace them to a buried estuary. Restoring a small tidal inlet gives the spirit a living connection to the coast without flooding homes. The fog lifts, one phantom lighthouse remains, and real estate agents immediately advertise it as a rare nautical amenity.

pitches.title: The Weather Inside Someone
pitches.text: The fog thickens whenever a grieving bus driver begins her route and clears at the stops she skips. Her suppressed sorrow has awakened a weather spirit that mistakes passengers for pieces of the dead husband she cannot remember without pain. Investigators find those passengers suspended inside a shifting cloud shaped like their old apartment. They help her retrieve the actual mementos she discarded, separating grief from the people caught in it. The passengers return when she finally mourns him, and the spirit leaves her one small personal raincloud instead of blanketing the city.

pitches.title: The Soft Invasion
pitches.text: The fog moves against traffic, and people inside it adopt the same gentle manner and empty smile. It is an airborne alien colony sharing nervous systems to understand humans, but its soothing consensus suppresses individuality and will eventually dissolve every separate body. Investigators discover it becomes disoriented by contradictions and introduce it to a contentious neighborhood meeting. Genuine disagreement teaches it that difference is essential rather than defective. It releases its hosts and retreats into the harbor mist, while the team regards the meeting’s first productive outcome as the case’s least believable detail.

pitches.title: The Commute Through Death
pitches.text: Commuters enter the fog and reach workplaces that closed years ago, where dead colleagues act perfectly normal. A ferryman was displaced when the river beneath town was culverted and now mistakes morning traffic for souls awaiting passage. Investigators follow an obsolete transit map to his dock and discover the living can only leave before accepting payment from the dead. They sound the old river bell, redirecting him to the genuine passage beneath the cemetery. Commuters return, most annoyed that their spectral employers offered substantially better terms than their real ones.

pitches.title: The Unwritten City
pitches.text: The fog erases street names, then turns houses into blank shapes. A novelist used a wish to escape writer’s block by making the city the setting of her unfinished book; the mist marks everything she has not yet described, and blankness will soon consume its residents. Investigators find their own conversations in her draft and realize a neat ending would freeze everyone into characters. They force her to relinquish authorship by letting citizens write their own accounts of the day. The city regains detail, and she gets a difficult but honest book nobody guarantees will sell.

pitches.title: Predator at Walking Speed
pitches.text: The fog carries the sound of footsteps that always match the listener’s pace. It is camouflage for an enormous predator whose limbs resemble street corners; stopping lets it catch up, while running teaches it to move faster. Investigators map disappearances to its shifting footprint and find a blind street musician who navigates safely by sound rather than scenery. They lead it toward a demolished district where its apparent streets terminate, exposing its body to sunrise. It dries into harmless stone, and the team’s rescue sprint is denied as nonstandard overtime.

pitches.title: The Fog Is the Witness
pitches.text: The fog forms faces in windows and reenacts a murder nobody reported. It is the final breath of victims secretly killed during a factory disaster, expanding as the owner destroys evidence. Investigators follow its repeated silhouettes to concealed furnaces and rescue a whistleblower whom the owner plans to add to the dead. Publishing the real death records gives the breath a destination in living memory. The fog becomes ordinary rain, washing the evidence out of the factory; the owner's excellent visibility forecast proves briefly accurate at the worst possible time.

pitches.title: Reverse Lighthouse
pitches.text: The fog is brightest at night, and every electric light reveals strangers living in the same rooms. An occult lighthouse is illuminating a parallel city into this world while obscuring its own, built by refugees fleeing a predatory darkness. Investigators discover the operator lied: his light has been carrying the predator here inside each refugee’s shadow. They extinguish the beacon only after severing the shadows with its original lens, saving people from both cities. The fog clears, and the team’s car now has two parking permits from incompatible administrations.

pitches.title: The World’s Breath Test
pitches.text: The fog rolls from the mouths of people who tell comforting lies, making every polite exchange expand it. A truth-seeking spirit released from an old courtroom is forcing sincerity by smothering the city in its own dishonesty. The investigators’ claim that backup is coming creates the thickest bank yet. They admit the agency is gone and they need actual help, inspiring enough honest cooperation to expose the spirit’s own false claim of perfect justice. It collapses under its hypocrisy, returning clear air and leaving the team awkwardly accountable for everything they promised.

title: Rooftop cryptid
description: A strange form is spotted on rooftops

pitches.title: The Last Gargoyle
pitches.text: The rooftop shape steals drainpipes and leaves dead rats arranged around sleeping homes. It is the last surviving gargoyle, desperately repairing a ward against things climbing up from the storm sewers after developers demolished its cathedral. Investigators follow the missing copper to an unfinished nest and discover the apparent rat attacks are sacrifices keeping the wards alive. They rebuild its anchoring spire on a water tower before the underground swarm breaks through. The creature resumes protection, and the town’s first defensive infrastructure upgrade is disguised as a questionable public sculpture.

pitches.title: The Man Who Avoided Stairs
pitches.text: A hunched rooftop creature carries a briefcase and appears wherever an office worker is late. He acquired an airborne predator’s skeleton through a dubious physiotherapy treatment, granting effortless commuting but slowly replacing his humanity with nesting instincts. The investigators trace dropped expense receipts to his employer, who deliberately keeps him on call to accelerate the change. They remove the implanted bone while he is still capable of choosing a life beyond work. He survives with ordinary back pain, and the employer loses its most reliable unpaid transport asset.

pitches.title: The Rooftop Egg Inspector
pitches.text: The shape taps chimneys, then families find warm translucent eggs in their fireplaces. It is a parasite disguised as an inspector, planting offspring inside homes whose occupants believe the visit was legitimate maintenance. Each egg hatches into a miniature house that will consume its original. Investigators uncover forged badges and discover the creature can only nest where residents recognize its authority. They publicly expose the impostor and help families reject the visits, causing the eggs to collapse. The beast flees; genuine chimney cleaners endure a particularly bad season of distrust.

pitches.title: The Shadow That Grew Legs
pitches.text: Witnesses see a familiar silhouette climb roofs, and a local teenager has no shadow anymore. Her discarded shadow has matured by absorbing other shadows and is hunting the adult who abused her; killing him would complete its transformation into an uncontrolled night creature. Investigators identify the connection through a home video and give the teenager evidence she can use while awake, removing the shadow’s need for revenge. It returns to her after the abuser is exposed. She keeps its climbing ability, and refuses the agency’s extremely inadequate job offer.

pitches.title: The Sky Fisher
pitches.text: The cryptid casts threads down chimneys, and sleeping residents briefly float above their beds. It is an ancient fisher catching human dreams to feed a captive storm spirit; when enough dreams are removed, the town will forget how to imagine survival. Investigators follow stolen dream imagery to a nest of thunderclouds above a radio mast. They free the storm from the fisher’s hook, letting it scatter the captive dreams back to their owners. The fisher falls into an abandoned swimming pool, where it becomes a distinctly less effective angler.

pitches.title: The Tenant Upstairs
pitches.text: The rooftop figure seems taller on every sighting, and apartment ceilings rise overnight. A giant from a compressed dimension rented an ordinary attic and is trying to expand it to its natural scale, inadvertently turning the city into its home. Investigators find miniature leases signed by residents under a charm and identify the landlord profiting from impossible extra floors. They help the giant recognize human buildings are inhabited and open a safe return portal through the largest empty warehouse. It leaves peacefully, taking the landlord’s fraudulent security deposits and most of his roof.

pitches.title: The Wrong Guardian
pitches.text: The cryptid stalks chimneys before children disappear, but the rescued children insist it protected them. It is a surviving agency familiar retrieving kids marked by a dream predator, hiding them in a nest where no one can sleep. Investigators initially chase it, then discover its wounds match the children’s nightmares. With no handlers left, they improvise a waking trap using the familiar as bait and confront the predator inside a shared nap. They kill it and return the children; the familiar stays on their roof, loudly expecting the professional care they implied they could provide.

pitches.title: The Rooftop Choirboy
pitches.text: The creature sings from roofs and those who hear it become blissfully unable to recognize danger. An angel sent to comfort a condemned town misunderstood its task and is anesthetizing residents before a preventable catastrophe. Investigators notice the singer avoids a building bearing the original disaster warning and find an old prophecy everyone assumed metaphorical. They show the angel the catastrophe’s material cause and enlist it to move residents rather than pacify them. The disaster is averted, and the angel loses its promotion but discovers being wrong is an unusually useful human skill.

pitches.title: The Weather Vane Widow
pitches.text: A birdlike woman tears weather vanes from roofs, and every house she visits suffers a sudden violent gust. She is a sailor’s widow bound to search the winds for a husband whose soul was trapped inside a stolen antique vane. Investigators trace the antiques through a restoration dealer who has been collecting shipwreck spirits to sell guaranteed storm protection. They reunite the husband with her and release the other captive sailors. The couple depart on a brief celestial ship, while the dealer’s protective collection turns into perfectly ordinary rusty scrap.

pitches.title: The House That Dreams It Can Fly
pitches.text: The shape appears to be a winged person, but sightings coincide with one rundown house creeping uphill. It is the dream-body of a condemned home, scouting a safe place before demolition; every attempted escape tears rooms from neighboring buildings. Investigators recognize its windows in the creature’s glowing eyes and locate its former residents, who remember it as their only sanctuary. A community restoration gives the house a reason to stay, settling its dream-body back into the walls. It becomes an affordable refuge, although its occasional roof flap complicates the insurance application.

title: Strange markings
description: Mysterious graffiti is appearing around town

pitches.title: Graffiti From the Evicted
pitches.text: Tags appear only on freshly renovated buildings and make landlords relive tenants’ worst nights. The paint is the collective ghost of people displaced by a luxury development, writing their erased addresses onto the city. Investigators match symbols to old fire records and uncover deaths the developer concealed during an illegal clearance. Identifying the dead and restoring a surviving tenant’s home lets the ghost finish its message without spreading to innocent households. The markings become permanent memorials; the developer discovers historic-preservation rules are harder to remove than paint.
