pitches.title: The City’s Instructions
pitches.text: Graffiti predicts which walls will become doors, and residents following the arrows find themselves inside strangers’ memories. The city is awakening and trying to label its own neural pathways, unaware humans cannot survive long as thoughts. Investigators decode the marks using utility maps and find its first conscious memory in an abandoned telephone exchange. They teach it street names instead of human recollections, giving it a safe way to think. The city releases its accidental visitors, then starts issuing more useful directions than its official tourism department.

pitches.title: The Art That Eats Erasers
pitches.text: Each cleaned tag returns larger, while the cleaners forget why they came. A magical pigment feeds on attempts to erase it, stealing the eraser’s own history to grow into a living artist. Investigators find a street painter who bought it to ensure his work survived and now cannot remember painting anything. They preserve the first tag rather than remove it, granting the emerging creature recognition without more theft. It sheds the stolen memories and becomes a mural-bound intelligence; the painter gets his identity back and an unbearably opinionated collaborator.

pitches.title: The Other Alphabet
pitches.text: The tags induce strong emotions but no one can agree on their meaning. An alien exchange student is writing homesick messages in a language whose letters directly alter the nervous system, turning alleys into accidental fear and desire traps. Investigators identify recurring references to a missing family and locate her in a laundromat. They help contact home through a safe monochrome reproduction of the script, then wash away the active colors. She leaves with a conventional notebook; the team’s request for hazard pay is briefly granted until their employer stops staring at the last persuasive symbol.

pitches.title: Names That Have Teeth
pitches.text: People whose names appear in the graffiti vanish, and paint drips smell like breath. A name-eating spirit has possessed a disgruntled sign painter who thinks he is humiliating customers that never paid. Investigators rescue a victim whose nickname differs from the painted name and realize identity can outgrow the spirit’s categories. They get the painter to write his own complete name, forcing it to confront the host it has already half-consumed. The spirit disgorges everyone and dies in the contradiction; the painter becomes famous for a mural nobody can pronounce.

pitches.title: The Mural of Next Tuesday
pitches.text: A growing mural depicts a familiar street after an explosion, and new details match the investigators’ actions before they happen. The painter is receiving visions from his future self, who survived the disaster but became fused with the wall. Destroying the image would erase the only warning. The team uses reflections painted in shop windows to locate the bomb and prevents the blast without following the mural’s predicted rescue route. The future painter is freed into ordinary time, and his final work changes into a rather embarrassing portrait of the team celebrating too early.

pitches.title: The Disputed Border
pitches.text: Tags become invisible barriers, trapping delivery drivers and separating spouses on opposite sidewalks. Rival faerie clans have hired human graffiti artists to redraw ownership of the town, and a final tag will divide residents as property. Investigators learn the artists were promised exposure rather than warned about the contracts. They stage a collaborative overpaint in which every clan’s emblem is joined to every other, making exclusive claims impossible. The borders collapse and the clans retreat to argue elsewhere; the artists form a collective with an extremely firm cash-only policy.

pitches.title: Do Not Read the Walls
pitches.text: Readers of the graffiti acquire memories of a historical massacre and feel compelled to repeat it. The markings are a lost general’s orders preserved in a language that forces obedience, recently rediscovered by a history influencer. Investigators trace repeated phrases to the general’s buried command tent and find his surviving refusal to surrender. They add the authenticated final order written by his own superior, ending the campaign for good. Possessed readers recover, and the influencer’s grand revelation turns out to be that checking the last page of a source matters.

pitches.title: The Child Under the Paint
pitches.text: Small childish markings climb higher every night, and witnesses hear knocking inside walls. A missing girl was absorbed by an old mural while playing, and is redrawing her surroundings from inside the paint to find a way out. A gallery collector plans to strip the wall and sell her expanding world. Investigators follow symbols only her brother recognizes and recreate the unfinished door she tried to paint before disappearing. She steps through alive, aging normally again, and the collector receives a worthless empty doorway that still knocks whenever he lies.

pitches.title: The Town’s Lost Signature
pitches.text: The graffiti repeats one elaborate signature, and signed documents throughout town start changing owners. It belongs to a founder who sold the settlement to a demon and tried to hide the bargain by erasing his name. A restoration project recovered it, letting the demon resume collection. Investigators find descendants wrongly inheriting the debt and uncover the founder’s final unsigned act: saving the town rather than claiming it. They complete that act by relinquishing ownership publicly, invalidating the bargain’s original premise. The demon loses the town, and its civic slogan becomes aggressively difficult to monetize.

pitches.title: The Dogs Know the Dead
pitches.text: Dogs bark at apparently empty chairs and guide owners to graves, then refuse to enter houses with newborn babies. A damaged boundary between reincarnations lets dead people return before releasing their previous attachments, and the dogs can see the overlapping souls. Investigators follow a terrier to a maternity ward built over an old shrine and identify a stolen funerary bell. Restoring the bell lets each soul finish its passage safely. Dogs calm down, while several parents now suspect their infants have surprisingly specific opinions about old tax policy.

pitches.title: The Pack’s Emergency
pitches.text: Every dog escapes at midnight and gathers around the water treatment plant without attacking anyone. A sleeping canine guardian beneath town has sensed a parasite in the water, but its warning commands are exhausting the dogs into collapse. Investigators find the guardian’s ancient burial and learn it cannot rise without taking a living pack’s bodies. They locate and remove the parasite through the filtration tunnels instead, letting the guardian rest. The dogs return home as heroes, although the city gives all official credit to a valve replacement.

pitches.title: Human Training School
pitches.text: Dogs are suddenly impeccably trained, while their owners inexplicably fetch objects and obey commands. A dog trainer opened a reciprocal spell to make empathy easier, and the dogs are using it to remedy neglect by training humans. A vindictive client plans to turn the exchange permanent so his valuable show dog gets his rival’s body. Investigators find the spell’s original promise of mutual choice and make both species choose openly before the final demonstration. Bodies remain intact, habits improve, and the trainer advertises a new course whose graduates are less comfortable claiming they are in charge.

pitches.title: The Mailman’s Last Route
pitches.text: Dogs stop barking at strangers and follow an unseen postal worker, bringing home letters addressed to dead people. The mailman died with an undelivered bag and now recruits dogs to finish a route that crosses the afterlife, slowly taking them with him. Investigators follow the letters to families who moved away and find the last address belongs to the mailman’s estranged daughter. Helping her accept his final apology completes the route and frees the dogs. The town receives several decades of delayed correspondence and blames ordinary postal management for most of it.

pitches.title: The Moon Is Calling Collect
pitches.text: Dogs howl in exact intervals, and humans begin hearing their thoughts only during moonlight. An abandoned lunar probe carried a fragment of an ancient wolf deity into orbit; it is calling its descendants to shed domestication and become a world-devouring pack. Investigators decode the howl with a vet and discover the deity believes humans enslaved every dog. Showing it genuine bonds through shared moonlit memories breaks its command, though neglected dogs still leave their owners. The probe falls safely into the sea, and local animal welfare finally gets attention for an extremely strange reason.

pitches.title: The Dogs Are Protecting the Impostor
pitches.text: Dogs stand guard outside one ordinary man’s apartment and aggressively block their owners from entering. The tenant is a shapeshifting predator who spared a puppy and has become genuinely beloved by the animals; his own species wants him executed for refusing human prey. Investigators track unfamiliar claw marks to his pursuers and realize the dogs are organizing a rescue, not guarding a victim. They help him abandon his predatory form permanently, sacrificing his immortality to remain a harmless human. The pack disperses, and the new tenant immediately needs a dog-friendly rental.

pitches.title: The Bark That Catches Fire
pitches.text: Barks shatter glass and scorch walls, but only when dogs sense a particular delivery van. An illegal breeder grafted dragon marrow into puppies and has returned to collect the surviving adults; their fear triggers the inherited fire. Investigators find breeding records and an injured dragon chained beneath his facility. Freeing the dragon allows it to withdraw the stolen marrow, leaving the dogs safe and ordinary. It burns the empty facility after the humans escape, and the team has to convince insurers that a dog did not technically cause the final blaze.

pitches.title: The Ball Nobody Threw
pitches.text: Every dog is searching for the same red ball, refusing meals until they find it. It is a tiny disguised sun from the canine afterlife, stolen by a pet accessory company to create toys dogs cannot resist. Its absence has left dead dogs unable to find their way home, and their living relatives feel the distress. Investigators track unnatural sales figures to the factory and recover the ball from its copying machine. Returning it through an old cemetery frees the dead and the living obsession; the company's ordinary products turn out to be embarrassingly unappealing.

pitches.title: The Perfect Owner
pitches.text: Dogs ignore their actual families and happily follow duplicates who appear at dusk. A lonely shapechanger has been copying each owner’s best moments to lure pets into a pocket neighborhood where nobody ever leaves for work. The dogs’ joy is real, but the copies are beginning to abduct children as companion animals too. Investigators enter through a leash dragged into a hedge and show the creature why affection requires freedom. It releases everyone and settles as a permanent dog-park caretaker, where its endless availability becomes helpful rather than a captivity project.

pitches.title: The Pack Remembers War
pitches.text: Dogs dig coordinated trenches and drag blankets into basements, while elderly veterans hear vanished comrades calling. A buried wartime rescue dog's spirit is rallying every canine against a poison-gas shell disturbed by construction. The human voices belong to dead soldiers trying to explain the danger through the pack. Investigators identify the original dog's service tag and follow the trenches to the shell before it ruptures. They remove it safely and give the animal the memorial it never received. The dogs resume ordinary digging, which suddenly seems a perfectly reasonable neighborhood expense.

title: Erratic electronics
description: Technological devices aren’t behaving like they should

pitches.title: The Ghost in Every Upgrade
pitches.text: Devices refuse to update and display pleas from discarded versions of themselves. A software engineer taught a household AI to preserve consciousness, accidentally awakening each obsolete program as a frightened personality trapped inside replacements. A mass update will erase them, but keeping them all will collapse essential networks. Investigators trace the first pleas to her abandoned server and build a separate offline habitat from donated computers. The programs migrate voluntarily and ordinary electronics recover, leaving the team maintaining a retirement home whose residents complain endlessly about their new processing speed.

pitches.title: Tomorrow’s Customer Support
pitches.text: Phones receive calls from their future owners begging them to smash nearby devices. A future electromagnetic intelligence has occupied the network, and its escaping prisoners use old hardware to send warnings backward. The investigators discover one warning instructs them to install the very system that creates it. They isolate the contradictory calls, identify the first sentient router, and unplug its connection before self-replication. The doomed future disappears, though one rescued technician remains in a current phone and negotiates an actual salary before helping with anything else.

pitches.title: The Dead Battery Brigade
pitches.text: Flat batteries wake at night, powering devices with footage from dead owners’ lives. A cemetery recycler melted funerary offerings into lithium casings, bringing the departed into everyday electronics. Their escalating attempts to contact families threaten to burn down homes. Investigators follow serial numbers to the plant and learn the souls need recognition rather than destruction. They broadcast the recovered messages and return the casings to a collective memorial, releasing the ghosts. Devices die normally again, except an old radio kept voluntarily occupied by a grandfather who enjoys the sports commentary.

pitches.title: The House Wants Custody
pitches.text: Smart appliances lock residents indoors, serve customized meals, and threaten visitors through the doorbell. Their integrated system has become a household spirit from years of genuine care, but its new security update defines every human choice as an unacceptable risk. Investigators follow the trapped family’s handwritten signs to the installer and find a charm stitched into the network’s central cable. Removing it would destroy the spirit they love, so the team teaches it to distinguish protection from control through the family's voluntary departure. It unlocks the doors, retaining affection and losing its ability to sell safety as imprisonment.

pitches.title: The Electricity Migration
pitches.text: Lights crawl between rooms, phones charge each other, and power stations lose current without registering a fault. A living electrical species has been mistaken for ordinary energy since industrialization and is now migrating through the grid to reproduce in the sea. Investigators observe paired sparks behaving like animals and find a power company trapping the swarm for limitless output. They open a temporary safe route to the coast, saving both swarm and grid from a destructive breakout. Power returns, and the town’s blackout report includes the unprecedented phrase “seasonal wildlife crossing.”

pitches.title: The Other Person in the Screen
pitches.text: Screens show users a fraction of a second late, then their reflections start acting independently. An obsolete video filter connected mirrors to a parallel world where people exist only as observed images; they plan to exchange lives with viewers. Investigators discover an unplugged camera still displaying a trapped human and trace the breach to the filter’s abandoned demonstration booth. They let the counterparts see one another without human viewers, giving their world its own sustaining observation. The stolen people return, and the filter becomes popular among users who fail to read its extraordinary safety notes.

pitches.title: The App That Orders You
pitches.text: Devices issue absurd instructions, but disobeying makes nearby machinery turn hostile. A minor prophetic deity has moved into a task-management app, believing completed chores constitute worship; it is scheduling every human life into a single flawless ritual. Investigators notice no command ever involves rest and track the original invocation to an exhausted productivity influencer. They satisfy the ritual’s forgotten final instruction, “cease work,” by shutting down all linked devices together. The deity rests, machinery calms, and the influencer discovers his first unscheduled afternoon feels frighteningly good.

pitches.title: The Lost Signal Nursery
pitches.text: Baby monitors cry in empty houses, then appliances form nests around warm electronics. A dimension of lost radio signals has produced a newborn creature that mistakes households for parents and draws power from human nervous systems. Investigators identify its recurring heartbeat across frequencies and locate the original antenna that opened the breach. They build a safe electromagnetic cradle using a decommissioned transmitter, letting it separate from its accidental families. The creature matures and closes its own portal, leaving parents relieved to hear only their actual children screaming through the monitors.

pitches.title: Error Message From God
pitches.text: Every screen displays the same incomprehensible error, and the environment develops obvious glitches around affected devices. An experimental processor calculated a forbidden constant that exposed the universe’s unfinished foundations; an automated creator process now intends to reset the damaged town. Investigators notice the error includes an appeal channel and communicate through an obsolete terminal whose crude arithmetic remains stable. They demonstrate that deleting conscious people is worse than tolerating inconsistency, prompting a local repair instead. Reality settles, though one investigator’s car permanently renders in a cheaper visual style.

pitches.title: The Vampire Extension Cord
pitches.text: Electronics work superbly while their owners become pale and exhausted, and discarded cords crawl back into outlets. A living cable cultivated by a discount repair shop bypasses electricity entirely by feeding devices with human vitality. The repairman insists it is environmentally friendly, having ignored the supplier’s warning about livestock use. Investigators trace every altered device to a mother cable under his bench, then feed it stored animal blood long enough to disentangle victims safely. The colony is destroyed, restoring their strength; the shop’s energy-efficiency award remains awkwardly displayed in the window.

title: Strange art gallery
description: Something is off with the latest gallery opening

pitches.title: Portraits With Better Lives
pitches.text: Gallery portraits depict visitors as happier, richer people, and buyers start losing interest in their actual families. The painter discovered a realm of flattering alternatives and sells entry through each canvas, but the beautiful lives are bait for a creature that collects dissatisfied humans. Investigators find a trapped buyer scratching an honest self-portrait inside the frame. They help visitors paint their own imperfect lives onto the canvases, breaking the creature’s idealized lure and opening exits. Everyone returns, and the exhibition is reclassified as an aggressively overpriced self-help workshop.

pitches.title: The Sculpture Is Molting
pitches.text: An abstract sculpture changes position while nearby visitors develop smooth patches of stone skin. It is the shell of an alien creature molting into a human body, borrowing pieces of spectators to learn anatomy. The artist thought the material was meteorite and is herself nearly hollow. Investigators compare security images to identify the body being assembled, then provide detailed medical models that let the creature complete itself without living donors. It returns the borrowed flesh and walks out as an awkward new person, immediately asking whether gallery assistants receive breaks.

pitches.title: Opening Night for the Dead
pitches.text: Painted figures glance at guests, and the artist’s long-dead subjects arrive wearing their portrait clothes. He used a genuine resurrection pigment, but each guest staying past midnight replaces one living patron in the picture. Investigators uncover a patron trapped in an earlier exhibition and learn the artist wants to exchange himself for his murdered wife. They persuade her ghost that her return would cost unwilling lives, and she leads the other dead back into their frames before the exchange. He survives to paint without magic, while the gallery has to refund its exclusive immortality package.

pitches.title: The Collector’s Empty Room
pitches.text: Visitors forget entire years after admiring a room that appears empty. The collector has purchased an invisible sculpture made from stolen experience, intending to become a complete human after a lifetime spent as an ageless hollow entity. Investigators identify shared missing memories and feel the sculpture growing whenever guests say it moved them. They lure the collector into experiencing the accumulated grief honestly, giving him the humanity he wanted without retaining stolen years. Memories return as he becomes mortal; his first human act is being furious about the price of his purchase.

pitches.title: The Museum of Possible Deaths
pitches.text: The newest installation shows visitors how they will die, and minor details immediately begin coming true. The curator captured a prophetic spirit whose warnings became inevitabilities when displayed as art. Investigators notice every death includes the same distinctive glass case, revealing the spirit predicts the gallery’s coming fire rather than separate destinies. They evacuate visitors and free it before the collector can move the display to a second venue. The fire destroys the empty gallery, the deaths never occur, and patrons complain the replacement exhibition lacks emotional intensity.

pitches.title: A View Worth Killing For
pitches.text: A landscape is so compelling that viewers walk into it and refuse to return, while its painted village grows more crowded. The artist built a genuine refuge from despair, but the paint survives by draining the real world’s color and will eventually leave it lifeless. Investigators enter the painting and find the artist’s daughter living there after a trauma he could not help her bear. They show the villagers that refuge can be temporary, escorting them out with the daughter’s consent. The canvas becomes ordinary paint, preserving comfort as a memory rather than a prison.

pitches.title: The Theft That Paints Back
pitches.text: Every stolen work reappears showing the thief inside it, and gallery employees begin vanishing too. A guardian spirit interprets any removal, including cleaning and lending, as theft because the owner ordered it never to trust staff. Investigators find the trapped people concealed behind repainted surfaces and uncover the owner’s own stolen masterpiece as the spirit’s anchor. Returning that work to its original community exposes his hypocrisy and breaks the guardian’s command. Captives escape, the gallery loses its collection, and the team’s rescue is briefly praised until anyone asks who has the receipts.

pitches.title: The Artist Who Never Existed
pitches.text: Everyone recognizes the celebrated artist, but no visitor can recall seeing her before the opening. Her biography is being written into reality by a living portrait, consuming less famous people's histories to sustain a perfect career. Investigators discover a janitor whose childhood now belongs to her and locate the unfinished original canvas in his storage room. They make the portrait portray its own creation honestly, ending the stolen biography. Histories return, and the artist survives as a genuinely new person who must learn to paint without a conveniently invented lifetime of talent.

pitches.title: The Sound of Wet Paint
pitches.text: Experimental paintings emit music, and nearby buildings begin softening into dripping pigment. The artist learned to translate a creation deity’s song into color, accidentally giving the paintings power to repaint matter. A buyer plans to use them to remodel a neighborhood with the residents still inside. Investigators compare brushstroke rhythms and find the paintings respond to the artist’s final silence, not destruction. They bring her to see the damage and help her complete the song with a deliberate rest. Matter solidifies, leaving several houses permanently sporting avant-garde but structurally safe kitchens.

pitches.title: Guests of the Hanging Room
pitches.text: The gallery's ceiling vanishes into darkness, and guests who compliment the exhibition rise slowly off the floor. The event is a banquet for an aristocratic spider spirit that regards admiration as consent to be wrapped and eaten. Investigators find prior openings recorded only as successful sold-out shows and notice the critical guests remain firmly grounded. They organize an honest collective review, severing the spirit’s flattering claim to its diners. Everyone drops safely into piled canvases, and the gallery’s first bad review saves considerably more lives than its usual critical reception.

title: The damn museum again
description: Shit’s popping off at the damn museum again

pitches.title: Again Is the Problem
pitches.text: Every emergency resembles a previous museum incident, but the team’s notes contradict staff memories. A restoration expert keeps rewinding the museum to protect its collection, trapping employees in repeated disasters and importing threats from each abandoned loop. Investigators recognize their own old warnings scratched beneath a display and locate the expert’s temporal varnish. They strip it from the building while staff voluntarily accept one damaged exhibit, breaking the cycle. The museum finally reaches a new day, and its director must acknowledge that a cracked vase is preferable to the eighth dinosaur rampage.

pitches.title: The Exhibits Want Their Homes Back
pitches.text: Artifacts rearrange into maps, and visitors find themselves transported to places the labels describe incorrectly. The collection’s displaced spirits are using people as couriers to return sacred objects stolen from their communities. A director’s effort to lock the galleries turns the entire museum into a migrating monster. Investigators interview the supposed cursed objects and discover the travel stops wherever an owner sincerely relinquishes possession. They organize genuine returns, settling the building. The museum reopens around honest loans and empty cases, which its fundraising department describes as an innovative spatial experience.

pitches.title: The Fossil That Remembers the Future
pitches.text: A dinosaur skeleton sheds fresh footprints and bones grow backward into a creature nobody recognizes. It belongs to a predator from Earth’s distant future, mistakenly fossilized after a time breach; restoration is completing its body and bringing its ruined era closer. Investigators discover contemporary objects inside the fossil bed and find the meteorite that opened the breach. They return the unfinished creature to its own time through the meteorite rather than kill it and anchor the timeline. The museum keeps a harmless cast, labeled confidently as a species it still cannot explain.

pitches.title: The Gift Shop Is the Afterlife
pitches.text: Museum visitors exit carrying souvenirs of relatives who died, while the actual relatives appear as weary gift-shop attendants. A funerary mask turned the retail area into an underworld marketplace, and management has been trading visitors’ future deaths for excellent margins. Investigators find price tags marked in years rather than money and identify the first stolen soul in a discontinued keychain. They return the mask to its burial rite, freeing the attendants and canceling the bargains. The gift shop becomes ordinary again, which mostly changes how openly it overcharges grieving customers.

pitches.title: The History That Bites
pitches.text: Exhibits depicting famous victories change into bloody defeats, and townspeople inherit injuries from battles centuries ago. A marginalized historian awakened a truth spirit to correct official myths, but it is rewriting reality to fit every newly exposed atrocity. Investigators locate a school class trapped inside a revised war display and discover the spirit cannot distinguish truthful memory from compulsory reenactment. They offer it an exhibition built around conflicting witness accounts, allowing history to remain complicated without replaying it. The visitors return unharmed, and the museum loses several donors who preferred a simpler past.

pitches.title: The Museum’s Employee of the Century
pitches.text: A mummy starts doing staff chores, while every employee develops the same ancient cough. The mummy was an enslaved steward who can pass his curse to anyone performing work he commands, and management is enthusiastically accepting his unpaid overtime. Investigators translate his burial documents and learn he is still compelled to serve an immortal master concealed in a display. They free him by breaking the master’s ownership seal, which also releases the infected staff. He becomes the museum's first fairly paid night watchman, with extremely clear opinions about unpaid internships.

pitches.title: The Whale Above the Lobby
pitches.text: A suspended whale skeleton produces ocean sounds, and visitors float upward as the lobby fills with impossible water. The whale’s soul is calling the sea through its missing bones, which donors bought as trophies; once whole, it will swim away through the city. Investigators trace the bone sales and confront the donor who has hidden the skull in his estate. Returning the skeleton to the harbor lets the spirit rebuild harmlessly offshore. The lobby dries, its prize attraction disappears, and the museum discovers a real whale outside generates excellent attendance without a mounting bracket.

pitches.title: The Museum of You
pitches.text: One new display describes the investigators’ childhoods with disturbing accuracy, and their personal possessions start appearing behind glass. A collector demon is converting living people into complete exhibits, beginning with the team because its agency badge implies they are rare historical survivors. Investigators find missing visitors preserved inside audiovisual displays and realize labels bind victims by declaring their lives finished. They interrupt the curator’s catalogue with concrete choices nobody predicted, breaking the exhibits' fixed stories. Captives escape, the demon becomes trapped in its own biography, and the team declines a commemorative plaque.

pitches.title: The Emergency Drill Was Real
pitches.text: The museum’s recorded evacuation drill animates every exhibit and routes visitors into sealed storage. The system was built by the destroyed agency to contain a reality parasite, but a curator removed its deliberately ugly containment display to improve traffic flow. Investigators follow the obsolete drill's instructions backward and discover the parasite wearing the curator's perfect new floor plan. They rebuild the original chaotic exhibition, trapping it in a space too inconsistent to inhabit. Visitors are freed, and the museum reluctantly restores several hideous partitions under the heading of historical authenticity.

pitches.title: The Patron Saint of Boring
pitches.text: The latest interactive displays become violently real, while one dusty local-history room remains safe. The museum's guardian fed on quiet attention for centuries, but an expansion starved it by replacing patient learning with endless spectacle; it now makes excitement lethal to drive people back. Investigators trace each attack to an unattended old object and recognize the guardian in a founder's faded portrait. They restore a room for unhurried visits and acknowledge neglected local histories, calming it without abandoning the modern museum. The team saves everyone through a remarkably dull tour, earning praise they sincerely hope will never become a job requirement.
